original.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY
original.text:
Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or
knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any
person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or
preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit
an assault.
Explanation.—Mere words do not amount to an assault. But the words
which a person uses may give to his gestures or preparation such a
meaning as may make those gestures or preparations amount to an
assault.
Illustrations.
(a) A shakes his fist at Z, intending or knowing it to be likely that he
may thereby cause Z to believe that A is about to strike Z. A has committed
an assault.
(b) A begins to unloose the muzzle of a ferocious dog, intending or
knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause Z to believe that he is
about to cause the dog to attack Z. A has committed an assault upon Z.
(c) A takes up a stick, saying to Z, “I will give you a beating”. Here,
though the words used by A could in no case amount to an assault, and
though the mere gesture, unaccompanied by any other circumstances,
might not amount to an assault, the gesture explained by the words may
amount to an assault.
Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave
provocation.

phase11.final_answer: The key difference is that criminal force involves actual physical force, while assault involves the threat or apprehension of such force.
phase11.summary_answer: Criminal force involves the actual use of force against a person, while assault is the act of causing someone to apprehend that such force is about to be used against them.
phase11.detailed_answer: Criminal force is defined as the actual application of force against another person, whereas assault is characterized by gestures or preparations that lead a person to believe that force is imminent. Specifically, Section 130 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita states that an assault occurs when someone makes a gesture or preparation that causes another person to apprehend that they are about to face criminal force. In contrast, criminal force can be seen in actions that directly inflict harm or threaten harm, as illustrated in Section 129, where inciting a dog to attack someone constitutes the use of criminal force.

llm_evidence.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY
llm_evidence.text: Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault.

llm_evidence.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY
llm_evidence.text: Whoever makes any gesture, or any preparation intending or knowing it to be likely that such gesture or preparation will cause any person present to apprehend that he who makes that gesture or preparation is about to use criminal force to that person, is said to commit an assault. Explanation.—Mere words do not amount to an assault. But the words which a person uses may give to his gestures or preparation such a meaning as may make those gestures or preparations amount to an assault. Illustrations. (a) A shakes his fist at Z, intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause Z to believe that A is about to strike Z. A has committed an assault. (b) A begins to unloose the muzzle of a ferocious dog, intending or knowing it to be likely that he may thereby cause Z to believe that he is about to cause the dog to attack Z. A has committed an assault upon Z. (c) A takes up a stick, saying to Z, “I will give you a beating”. Here, though the words used by A could in no case amount to an assault, and though the mere gesture, unaccompanied by any other circumstances, might not amount to an assault, the gesture explained by the words may amount to an assault. Punishment for assault or criminal force otherwise than on grave provocation.

llm_evidence.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY
llm_evidence.text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting to commit theft on any property which that person is then wearing or carrying, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Assault or criminal force in attempt to wrongfully confine a person.

llm_evidence.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY
llm_evidence.text: A incites a dog to spring upon Z, without Z’s consent. Here, if A intends to cause injury, fear or annoyance to Z, he uses criminal force to Z. Assault.

llm_evidence.chapter_title: OF OFFENCES AFFECTING THE HUMAN BODY
llm_evidence.text: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, intending thereby to dishonour that person, otherwise than on grave and sudden provocation given by that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both. Assault or criminal force in attempt to commit theft of property carried by a person.
